$comment: The still set `pocctl bench --images` drives the detector over, and the provenance record for
WHY THIS SET IS ONE IMAGE AND WHY THAT IS HONEST. It exists so the detector can be TIMED:
`pocctl bench --images` opens a real ONNX Runtime session, drives it over the stills, and
writes the measured p50/p99 to <data-root>/detector-calibration.json, which is where
`pocctl preflight` reads the number its detector row multiplies by the declared frame
rate. A detection benchmark needs a labelled set and a licence per image; a TIMING set needs
a frame the detector can decode, and the repo already has one: frame 0 of
`testdata/injection-hostile.mp4`, whose row in testdata/labels.json records that it is
synthetic, that every pixel is a Go computation, and that no third-party material is in it.
WHAT IT DOES NOT DO. One negative frame cannot measure recall, and this manifest does not
claim it can: `boxes` is empty because nothing is in the frame, and the bench will say
`negative frame, nothing drawn, nothing there`. The false-positive rate over real footage
is a `pocctl bench --run` measurement over a finished run, and it stays NOT RUN until
somebody marks which of the model's boxes are really objects.
classes_file: not applicable: the classes come from the model's ONNX metadata, and this still set adds none of its own
boxes_file: not applicable: no box is annotated, and an empty list is a ground truth rather than a missing one
image_licence: the same licence as this repository. There is no rights holder to ask: the frame is generated locally by `go run ./cmd/injectionfixture`, contains no third-party footage, no downloaded source and no copyrighted asset. testdata/labels.json records the row and the SHA-256 below is that row's.
annotation_licence: the same licence as this repository, and the same reason: the annotations are the empty list this repository writes, over an image this repository drew.
attribution: none required. No licence here imposes an attribution condition.

images.original_url: generated locally by `go run ./cmd/injectionfixture`; no third-party material and no network are involved at any point
images.author: this repository
images.license: the same licence as this repository
images.note: frame 0 of the committed injection fixture. It is a colour-bar pattern with one filled rectangle crossing a line, so the detector has something to look at and nothing to find: a still set for TIMING does not need a real scene, and one for SCORING must not be this one.
